title: Zdzisław Beksiński — the nightmare painter who called his work optimistic
summary: A compact biography of Polish surrealist Beksiński: architect turned self-taught sculptor and painter, 'photographing dreams' in untitled Silent Hill-meets-Hellraiser landscapes, painting 14-hour standing sessions to loud music, and a life that tragically came to mirror his canvases. Useful context for dark surrealism and dystopian landscape art.
takeaways: Beksiński refused titles and explanations — meaning was left to the viewer
He worked to loud music for long standing sessions; ritual and soundtrack fueled output
Strong reference for desolate, architectural dreamscape aesthetics

title: Ink and pencil layering — iterative line-drawing loop with eraser passes
summary: A process clip of an ink drawing built through repeated pencil-plan, ink, erase cycles using Sennelier ink and Faber-Castell pencils. The caption's rhythm ('ink—pencil—eraser—…mistake—eraser') is the real lesson: drawing as patient iteration.
takeaways: Plan in pencil, commit in ink, erase, repeat — mistakes are part of the loop

title: Chris Wood light art — shifting glow from dichroic glass in motion
summary: A silent loop of shifting colored light and endless motion from light artist Chris Wood. Mood/visual reference without process detail.
takeaways: Reference for color-shifting light installations

title: Waterproof shower notes — capturing ideas that actually become projects
summary: A maker shows a shower wall covered in waterproof Post-it sketches and argues shower-captured ideas convert to real projects more often than notebook ideas — including procedurally generated brackets and a glueless snap-tab 3D-printed connector for recycled cardboard. Messy, but a real creative-capture habit with receipts.
takeaways: Put a capture surface where ideas show up (the shower), not where you think they should
Review old raw sketches — early versions often already contain the final solution
Flexing snap tabs into holes can join plastic to cardboard without glue

title: Blender painterly brush-stroke add-on — 3D animation that looks hand-painted
summary: Silent showcase of painterly 'art strokes' rendered in Blender using an add-on by @tim.dub.cg, giving 3D animation a brush-stroke, hand-painted look. The add-on isn't named beyond its creator's handle.
takeaways: Look up @tim.dub.cg for the stroke add-on
Painterly NPR strokes make 3D read as illustration

title: Handheld hyperlapse of New York — in-camera transitions, After Effects edit
summary: A New York hyperlapse built from thousands of handheld stills (shoot, step, shoot) over days of 15–25k steps, with every transition planned and executed while shooting, then assembled in After Effects.
takeaways: Handheld hyperlapse: fix a target point, shoot, take a step, repeat
Design transitions on location so the edit is mostly assembly
Expect thousands of frames per sequence — plan storage and stabilization

title: Medusa digital drawing — colorblind challenge on a sick day
summary: A silent digital-drawing clip of a Medusa piece made for a colorblind drawing challenge. Light inspiration; no process narration.
takeaways: Constraint challenges (e.g. colorblind palette) are a cheap way to break habits

title: Pendulum drawing machine — harmonograph kinetic sculpture with a rocking table
summary: A welded kinetic drawing machine (harmonograph) with four pendulums: two drive the pen in X and Y, and two more rock and rotate the drawing table to add chaos to the patterns. Shown mid-build ahead of an art show.
takeaways: Couple extra pendulums to the table, not just the pen, for richer figures
Shared rods between pendulums inject controlled chaos

title: Animatronic eye sculpture — hexagonal plate with moving eyes and macramé mandala
summary: A stage-design art piece: a grey hexagonal plate of moving animatronic eyes framed by a macramé mandala, conceived as a bridge between people and a moon deity. Built for an event production; silent showcase.
takeaways: Multiple synchronized moving eyes are an arresting focal element for stage/event decor

title: Oil glazing with Galkyd Lite and Gamsol — thin transparent color layers
summary: A three-step oil glaze: once the painting is fully dry, mix your color with Galkyd Lite and Gamsol to a thin, transparent consistency (more Gamsol for thinner), then brush it over the target area.
takeaways: Only glaze over completely dry paint
Galkyd Lite + Gamsol is the glazing medium; tune thinness with Gamsol

title: Brushstroke tattoo — 3D paint-stroke style in blue
summary: A tattoo shop reel of a 3D 'paint stroke' tattoo rendered in blue, mimicking thick brushstrokes on skin. Visual reference only.
takeaways: Reference for painterly, dimensional tattoo styles

title: David Ambarzumjan print signing — limited-edition art print shop reopening
summary: A silent clip of the artist signing limited-edition prints ahead of reopening his print shop. Mostly promotional; minimal content beyond the satisfying process.
takeaways: Limited-edition print runs as an artist revenue model

title: Visual interactive drumming — DIY audio-reactive light instrument
summary: A new-media piece by twentytwohalo where drum hits trigger synchronized light visuals — a DIY audiovisual instrument at the creative-coding/light-art intersection. Silent clip, no build details.
takeaways: Map percussive triggers to lighting for a performable visual instrument

title: Nihonga with silver leaf — Japanese painting reveal 'like magic'
summary: A silent reveal of a contemporary Japanese painting (nihonga) using mineral pigments and silver leaf, with the surface shifting under light. Visual reference for metallic-leaf techniques.
takeaways: Metal leaf changes with viewing angle — design for light, not just the image

title: Kim Rose blood-and-poison NFTs — artworks that age, die and are reborn
summary: Kim Rose made animated works from a mix of her own blood and poison; the NFTs are programmed to slow and darken over 100 years, die, glow gold for nine months, then be reborn. Shown at a solo show in New York.
takeaways: Programmable art can encode a lifecycle measured in decades
Unusual materials produce fluid movements paint can't

title: Felipe Pantone in Shanghai — 'Diagonal Reading, Stroboscopic Attention' install
summary: Installation footage of Felipe Pantone's solo show 'Diagonal Reading, Stroboscopic Attention, yet, Profound Oneness' at Gallery All, Shanghai (Nov 2023) — his signature gradient, optical, kinetic works.
takeaways: Reference for gradient/op-art color systems and stroboscopic visual effects

title: Large three-panel abstract pour — commissioned landscape triptych
summary: A throwback reel of a three-panel abstract landscape commission made with pouring medium and heavy paint. Silent; limited process insight.
takeaways: Triptych format for large commissioned abstract work

title: Pete Mauney 'folded time' — real-time Newark and LaGuardia air-traffic video
summary: Photographer Pete Mauney's video experiment over the New Jersey Turnpike: aircraft departing Newark and lining up for LaGuardia, all moving in real time, framed to feel like time folded. A study in finding new ways to look at an old subject.
takeaways: Re-shoot a familiar location in motion to reveal hidden patterns
Real-time multi-layer motion can feel like compressed time

title: Unconventional painting tools — sticks, glue, rocks and ink
summary: Alisha Taweel's case for painting with non-brush tools (a stick, glue, a rock and some ink) to discover watercolor textures and marks you'd never find otherwise.
takeaways: Swap the brush for found tools to break your default marks
Glue resists and stick lines give textures brushes can't

title: Salvador Dalí on hypnagogic images — 1971 Dick Cavett interview
summary: Dalí explains to Dick Cavett that his paintings aren't dreams but hypnagogic images — vivid images in the 10–15 minutes before sleep that he 'catches' and paints photographically, with no message or explanation.
takeaways: Dalí sourced imagery from the hypnagogic state just before sleep
Paint the image precisely; leave the meaning unexplained

title: Kintsugi sake-bottle repair — urushi lacquer joins, gold powder finish
summary: A traditional hon-kintsugi repair of a broken tokkuri (sake flask): crack-stopping and interior repairs are finished first because the narrow neck blocks later access, then shards are glued with mugi-urushi, squeeze-out is trimmed with a design knife, and seams are finished in keshifun gold powder.
takeaways: On narrow-necked vessels, repair the interior before bonding the shards
Mugi-urushi (wheat-flour lacquer) is the adhesive; trim squeeze-out by hand
Keshifun gold powder gives a soft matte finish on the seams

title: Blue Star — minimal geometric blue artwork for mood reference
summary: A minimal reel titled 'Blue Star' by tola.art with no description or narration; a geometric blue piece for visual reference.
takeaways: Mood reference only

title: James Stevens Curl on ornament — why art looks bolted onto modernist buildings
summary: Architectural historian James Stevens Curl argues sculpture and decoration were integral to architecture from Greece through Gothic, Renaissance, Rundbogenstil and Egyptian Revival, until modernism removed ornament entirely — so art now feels bolted on as an afterthought.
takeaways: Integrated ornament was the historical norm; its absence is the anomaly
Design decoration with the structure, not after it

title: Enchanted lamps — painting-style lamp product promo
summary: A meme-format promo for a shop selling painting-like lamps for a 'perfect study room'. No subject beyond the product pitch.
takeaways: Product ad, nothing to learn
drop_reason: pure self-promo with zero content (product ad)

title: Underwater cenote photography — 83 dives of reference-driven reshoots
summary: Josiah WG shows his process for an underwater photo book: scouting Yucatán cenotes on a road trip, then using those early shots as reference to reshoot scenes across 83 dives with better site knowledge and a clearer overarching theme. Includes a gear-shop shout-out.
takeaways: Use early scouting shots as references, then reshoot with a defined theme
Long-form projects (a book) justify dozens of returns to one location
